summary: Outbound conntrack table exhaustion on customer NAT causing intermittent TLS resets for streaming client sessions
description:
Issue summary: Customer on a private deployment reports intermittent TLS resets and streaming disconnections when clients open many short-lived streaming sessions. Impact: Multiple production services report increased 502/504 and client-side TLSBrokenPipe/connection reset errors; customer reports degraded UX for chat streaming and some failed model requests. Environment: Private deployment behind customer-managed NAT gateway in us-west-2; Redwood agents running on customer private VPC with egress through a single NAT appliance. Steps to reproduce:
1) From client fleet, open 500+ concurrent short-lived streaming connections to Redwood API over TLS, each lasting ~3-12 seconds and then closing.
2) Observe some fraction (~5-15%) of sessions fail mid-stream with TLS errors.
Observed behavior: Random TLS connection resets and TCP RSTs from gateway, followed by service-level 502s and client side errors. Kernel logs (customer NAT) show nf_conntrack table full messages. Expected behavior: Stable streaming connections without unexpected resets.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: conntrack table on customer NAT/edge device exhausted due to high ephemeral port churn from many short-lived TLS sessions. Evidence collected: customer provided dmesg output containing 'nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet', and conntrack counters showing high entries. Commands run by SRE: 'sudo conntrack -S' returned 65536 total entries and a high percent used; 'ss -tnp' on backend nodes showed many TIME_WAIT connections. Packet captures showed SYN/ACK then immediate RSTs when table hits limit. We also observed asymmetric behaviour when NAT mapping rotated; some return packets were dropped. Alternative hypotheses considered: firewall session timeout too low, buggy NAT appliance firmware. Customer hardware: vendor-branded NAT appliance with default conntrack size. Temporary mitigation applied: customer increased conntrack_max and reduced TCP TIME_WAIT reuse timeout on gateway, and we suggested enabling keepalives for long-running streams. Follow-ups: request for customer to upgrade NAT appliance firmware and implement sticky SNAT or larger pool of source IPs for egress to reduce mapping churn.
logs_and_snippets: Mar 12 14:23:01 nat-gw kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
tcpdump: 5000 packets from client_ip to api.redwood: TLS handshake; then RST after 5-10s
ss -s on backend: TCP: 3456 established, 789 in TIME-WAIT, many originators in CLOSE-WAIT
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports increased streaming errors starting 2026-03-12 13:40 UTC. Provided dmesg and conntrack output. Asked SRE to triage.

Ravi Patel (SRE): Confirmed 'nf_conntrack: table full' in customer's kernel logs. Hypothesis: high churn of short-lived TLS streams causing conntrack exhaustion on customer's NAT appliance. Requested temporary increase of conntrack_max and reduce TIME_WAIT timers.

Customer (Acme Financial): Increased conntrack_max to 200000 and applied recommended TIME_WAIT tuning. Observed immediate reduction in resets; still seeing ~1% errors under peak load. Customer will check NAT firmware and consider pool of SNAT IPs.
Ravi Patel (SRE): Recommended customer enable persistent connections/keepalive for streaming clients and implement SNAT IP pool or sticky SNAT. Opened INT-4021 to track internal guidance doc updates.
resolution: Workaround: Customer increased conntrack_max and adjusted TCP TIME_WAIT and established keepalive settings for streaming clients, which reduced error rate to acceptable levels. Permanent fix plan: customer to (1) upgrade NAT appliance firmware to address conntrack handling bugs, (2) allocate multiple SNAT IPs or use a load balancer that preserves source IP mapping, (3) implement connection pooling / longer-lived streams on client side. Redwood actions: publish conntrack troubleshooting checklist in Confluence, add guidance to private deployment onboarding docs, and add automated alert rule to detect 'nf_conntrack' kernel messages via agent logs.
